title: Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF) Communications Planner (I) (LtCol to Capt) NMOS (0602), DIR IC4
raw_text:
2. MOS 0603, Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF) Communications Planner (I)
(LtCol to Capt) NMOS (0602), DIR IC4

    a. Summary. MAGTF Communications Planners integrate and coordinate with
the plans sections or operations sections of their respective command. MAGTF
Communications Planners must identify and clearly translate communications
and Department of Defense Information Network Operations (DODIN Ops)
capabilities, limitations, and opportunities in all phases of the planning
cycle. They integrate DODIN Ops with cyberspace operations, specifically
focused on supporting defensive cyberspace operations and directing the
planning efforts of the systems planning and engineering cell in their
respective unit. The MAGTF Communications Planner will also plan, integrate,
and synchronize communications and DODIN Ops with other information related
capabilities such as electronic warfare, space operations, and offensive
cyberspace operations. Example billets are MEF G-6 (Ops, Plans) MEB G-6
(ops, plans), SPMAGTF (ops, plans), MEU (S-6), communications battalion (S-
3), MWCS (S-3).


                                             1-44                        Enclosure (1)
 1109                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must possess the PMOS of 0602.

        (3) Security requirement:         top secret with sensitive compartmented
information access eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the MAGTF Communications Planner Course
(M09DRX1) Twentynine Palms, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (i), Communications Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Communications Officer, 0602.

            (2) Communications Chief, 0699.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
